What the numbers say

For the session of Wednesday, October 28, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (101 Taiwan-listed names: the 100 largest companies by market value plus the 0050 ETF) as mixed. The TAIEX is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

58 of 101 tickers (57%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 88 of 101 (87%) above their 200-day average. Above 55% is the breadth the model requires, together with the benchmark above its 50-day average and volatility not high, for a risk-on reading. On the day 70 rose and 28 fell, with 3 unchanged; the median move was +1.35%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Optoelectronics had the strongest average move at +5.54% and Financials the weakest at −0.78%, a spread of 6.32 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.37 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

No ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30, and 3 at or above 70 (2412, 4938, 2892). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Summed over the 101 names with institutional data, foreign investors' five-day position is net buying of 248,988 lots and investment trusts' is net buying of 31,583 lots (one lot is 1,000 shares). The two groups are on the same side.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-27), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 47% to 57%, and the regime reading stayed mixed.
